findings.title: Session tokens are compared by reference, not value
findings.description: `session.token == token` compares Java references. Tokens parsed from an Authorization header will be different String instances from those stored when issued, so verify() returns null and every authenticated request is rejected.

findings.title: Expired sessions are never rejected
findings.description: `verify()` never checks `expiresAt`, so sessions remain valid indefinitely after the documented 12-hour lifetime and also accumulate forever.

findings.title: Admin authorization rejects every role
findings.description: `!role.equals("admin") || !role.equals("owner")` is always true: for any role, at least one comparison is false and negated. Thus requireAdmin() never allows an admin or owner.

findings.title: Missing or malformed Authorization header crashes request handling
findings.description: `bearerToken()` dereferences a null header or reads `parts[1]` without checking the header or its structure. A request with no Authorization header, an empty header, or only a scheme throws NullPointerException or ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning 401.

findings.title: Cache eviction does not select the least recently used item
findings.description: set() gets the first key from a HashMap iterator and calls it LRU eviction, but HashMap order is arbitrary and independent of `entry.used`; recently used entries can be evicted.

findings.title: sweep() mutates map while iterating and throws
findings.description: Removing keys with `entries.remove(code)` while iterating `entries.keySet()` throws ConcurrentModificationException on the first expired entry. The janitor thread then terminates, so future cache sweeps are not performed.

findings.title: Cache utilization is truncated to zero and divides by zero
findings.description: `entries.size() / limit * 100` performs integer division first, so any partial utilization reports 0%. If limit is 0, which Config.validate() allows, this throws ArithmeticException from /stats.

findings.title: Cache TTL is interpreted as seconds when configured in milliseconds
findings.description: `LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS` is documented as milliseconds but assigned directly to `cacheTtlSeconds`. For example, 300000 ms becomes 300000 seconds, retaining stale cache entries for about 83 hours.

findings.title: Several environment values are parsed without error handling
findings.description: Invalid LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS, LINKD_CACHE_SIZE, or LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT causes NumberFormatException to escape load(), aborting startup instead of using the documented working defaults.

findings.title: Invalid timeout is set to zero despite a log saying the default is kept
findings.description: The catch block prints `keeping default` but then assigns `cfg.timeoutMillis = 0`, not the initialized default of 10000. This can force invalid configuration handling to trigger unnecessarily.

findings.title: validate() always accepts invalid configuration
findings.description: The method accumulates problems and prints them, but unconditionally returns true. Main ignores the return value and starts with invalid settings, contrary to the fail-at-startup contract.

findings.title: File writers leak if writing fails
findings.description: exportCsv(), archiveAll(), and appendAudit() close their FileWriter only after successful writes. An IOException leaves the writer open; the same applies to archiveAll() at line 53 and appendAudit() at line 77.

findings.title: Snapshot rename result is ignored
findings.description: File.renameTo() returns false rather than throwing when it cannot move the temporary snapshot. The caller then believes writeSnapshot() succeeded, even though the destination may contain a stale or absent snapshot and the temporary file remains.

findings.title: equals() is overridden without hashCode()
findings.description: Link defines equality by code but leaves the default identity hash code. Java hash collections may treat equal links as unequal, violating the documented map/set use.

findings.title: Query parameters are not URL-decoded
findings.description: Query parsing uses getRawQuery() and leaves percent escapes encoded. A standard client sending `target=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com` therefore supplies an encoded string that fails the schema check; similarly encoded `code` and `next` values are misinterpreted.

findings.title: POST /links accepts null request fields and crashes
findings.description: Missing `target` or `owner` reaches Store.create()/Store quota logic. `target.startsWith(...)` dereferences null before a 400 response can be produced, and null owner is not represented as a valid owner.

findings.title: Redirect request without code throws
findings.description: `query(exchange).get("code")` returns null for a missing parameter; `code.toLowerCase()` dereferences it. The HTTP connection terminates with an exception rather than returning 404/400.

findings.title: Stats divide by zero when the store is empty
findings.description: Store.totalHits() is divided by Store.size(). With no links, size() is 0 and /stats throws ArithmeticException.

findings.title: Default CSV export name is not used consistently
findings.description: exportCsv() substitutes "links" for a null or empty name, but exportCsv's returned path is ignored and readReport() rebuilds the filename from the original name. With name missing, the server writes links.csv yet attempts to read `null.csv` or `.csv` and returns 500.

findings.title: Listing pagination accepts malformed offset/size and crashes
findings.description: offset and size are passed directly to Integer.parseInt without validation. Non-numeric values throw NumberFormatException, while negative values are passed to Store.page() and can cause index exceptions.

findings.title: Malformed TTL crashes link creation
findings.description: `Integer.parseInt(fields.get("ttl"))` is outside the try block and has no validation. A nonnumeric TTL throws NumberFormatException instead of returning 400.

findings.title: Link expiry condition is inverted
findings.description: `Instant.now().isBefore(link.expiresAt)` is true for an active link, so resolve() removes it and returns null. Expired links fall through and continue resolving. Every redirect therefore destroys a valid link and then fails.

findings.title: New owners trigger NullPointerException and partially create links
findings.description: `quota.get(owner) + 1` unboxes null for the first use of an owner, so almost every create() call throws. Since the link is already inserted at line 27, this also leaves the new link in the store despite the failed creation.

findings.title: page() sets an out-of-bounds end index
findings.description: When a page extends beyond the data, end is set to `all.size() + 1`, not `all.size()`. `subList` then throws IndexOutOfBoundsException; the common case of offset=0 with fewer than 20 links does this.

findings.title: Generated code can be shorter than eight hex digits and crashes
findings.description: Long.toHexString() omits leading zeroes. When the random long's first hex nibble is zero (about 1 in 16 calls), the string is shorter than 8 characters and `.substring(0, 8)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException.

findings.title: rename() validates the source code twice
findings.description: Both validation calls use `from`; the destination code is never validated. An invalid or empty destination can be installed, and renaming to the same existing code is treated as already in use.

findings.title: Deleting a link never restores its quota
findings.description: delete() removes the link but does not decrement the owner's quota entry, contrary to the documented quota-return behavior. Owner counts become permanently inflated after deletion.

findings.title: successRate() performs integer division before scaling
findings.description: `used / links.size() * 100` truncates the ratio to zero whenever fewer than 100% of links were followed, making /stats success_rate almost always 0 rather than a percentage.

findings.title: Leaderboard sorted ascending instead of most hits first
findings.description: The comparator uses `Long.compare(a.hits, b.hits)`, so top(n) returns the least followed links.

findings.title: byOwner() performs substring matching instead of exact ownership
findings.description: `link.owner.contains(owner)` returns records for every owner containing the requested owner as a substring, e.g. requesting `alice` also returns `alice2`; a null owner makes this NPE.

findings.title: findByCode() compares codes by reference
findings.description: `link.code == code` succeeds only for interned/reference-identical strings, not for two equal code values. Correct links are missed and the method returns null.

findings.title: extend() revives already expired links
findings.description: extend() does not check that `expiresAt` is still in the future. A link that has already expired, but not yet been swept, gets its expiry moved into the future despite the documented invariant that expiry is final.

findings.title: importAll() is advertised as atomic but is not
findings.description: The loop validates and stores each link as it goes. If validation fails later in the batch, all previously imported links remain, violating the either-none guarantee. It also does not validate target/owner or quota state.

findings.title: prune() mutates map while iterating and throws
findings.description: Removing codes from `links` while iterating `links.keySet()` throws ConcurrentModificationException on the first expired entry, rather than returning the number removed.

findings.title: Janitor mutates store map while iterating and dies
findings.description: Removing an expired code from `store.all()` while iterating the same keySet throws ConcurrentModificationException. Since the exception is outside the interrupted-loop handling, the janitor thread terminates permanently once a link expires.

findings.title: warmCache leaks worker threads and returns before work completes
findings.description: The method creates a fixed pool, submits tasks, and never calls shutdown/awaitTermination. It returns immediately rather than after warm-up finishes, and each invocation leaves eight non-daemon threads alive.

findings.title: countForOwner() unboxes a nullable Integer
findings.description: `store.quotas().get(owner)` returns null for an owner with no records. Returning it as `int` throws NullPointerException rather than reporting zero.

findings.title: Store maps are shared without synchronization
findings.description: The janitor mutates and iterates links through Store.all(), while handler methods can create, delete, resolve, page over, and aggregate the same HashMap. Concurrent put/remove/iteration can throw ConcurrentModificationException or corrupt and lose links; quota increments are also non-atomic.

findings.title: Janitor mutates a live HashMap during iteration and dies on exceptions
findings.description: The janitor repeatedly calls store.all(), iterates its key set, then removes directly from the returned map. If a handler creates/deletes concurrently, iteration can throw ConcurrentModificationException or get() can return null later. Even the janitor's own removal can throw CME on the following iteration. The exception is uncaught, so the janitor stops permanently.

findings.title: prune removes entries while iterating the same map
findings.description: prune iterates links.keySet() and calls links.remove(code) inside the loop. As soon as more than one entry exists and an expired key is removed, the next iterator access throws ConcurrentModificationException.

findings.title: Internal mutable maps escape Store
findings.description: all() returns the live links map and quotas() returns the live quota map. Worker iterates and mutates links through all(), while callers can read quota without Store coordination. This bypasses any later synchronization added to Store and perpetuates the races.

findings.title: Session map is not safe for concurrent access
findings.description: issue(), verify(), revoke(), and sessionCount() share a plain HashMap. A verify() iteration can run concurrently with issue() or revoke(), causing ConcurrentModificationException or map corruption. Returned Session objects are also unsafely published.

findings.title: peek, stats, and utilization bypass Cache synchronization
findings.description: get/set/delete/sweep synchronize the Cache object, but peek reads entries without a lock, stats reads the non-volatile long hits, and utilization reads entries.size() without a lock. This can produce stale or torn values, and map reads can race with structural modifications.

findings.title: sweep removes map entries during iteration
findings.description: sweep iterates entries.keySet() and calls entries.remove(code) directly. After the first expired entry is removed, the next iteration can throw ConcurrentModificationException. Since this runs on the janitor and is not caught, the janitor can terminate.

findings.title: Cache singleton initialization has a check-then-act race
findings.description: getInstance() checks instance == null and assigns a non-volatile static field without synchronization. Concurrent first calls can create and return distinct Cache instances, splitting cache state and statistics.

findings.title: warm uses a non-atomic peek-then-set race
findings.description: warm() checks whether a code is absent, then calls set() in a separate step. A delete, replace, or eviction between the two calls can be overwritten or a deleted code can be inserted back into the cache.

findings.title: Metrics.created is incremented without synchronization
findings.description: addCreated() does not synchronize while snapshot() does. Multiple concurrent creators can lose increments, and snapshot() has no happens-before edge for created, so it can observe a stale or torn long.

findings.title: warmCache submits work without waiting or shutting down the pool
findings.description: warmCache() creates a fixed thread pool, submits tasks, and returns immediately despite documenting that it returns after the probes finish. Tasks may still be running, and each call can leave idle non-daemon threads that are never shut down.

findings.title: Shared SimpleDateFormat is not thread-safe
findings.description: Export.STAMP is a mutable SimpleDateFormat shared by concurrent calls to exportCsv(). Concurrent format() calls can corrupt the formatter's internal calendar and return wrong timestamps or throw runtime exceptions.

findings.title: Session tokens are predictable and logged
findings.description: Session tokens are generated from java.util.Random rather than a cryptographically secure source, and line 40 prints the token to standard output. Anyone able to observe generated outputs or logs can predict or recover future tokens and impersonate sessions.

findings.title: Bearer token verification uses reference equality
findings.description: verify() compares session.token == token. A token parsed from an Authorization header is a different String object, so valid user credentials are rejected and the authentication control is nonfunctional on all HTTP paths.

findings.title: Expired sessions are still accepted
findings.description: Session has expiresAt, but verify() never checks it. Consequently, a stolen or otherwise retained session token remains valid indefinitely after its intended 12-hour lifetime unless the process is restarted or the token is explicitly revoked.

findings.title: Admin authorization trusts a client-supplied header
findings.description: Any authenticated user can call /admin/quotas with X-Admin: true. The authenticated session's role is never checked, so the endpoint's claimed administrator-only boundary is bypassable.

findings.title: Link creation uses caller-controlled owner
findings.description: Although the request is authenticated, owner is taken from the query string rather than the session. A user can create links attributed to another owner and manipulate per-owner quota accounting for that owner.

findings.title: Any session can delete anyone's link
findings.description: The DELETE handler ignores the authenticated session and calls Store.delete directly. Once a code is known, any authenticated user can remove it. Combined with /report, all codes are discoverable.

findings.title: Report endpoint exports all users' links for any session
findings.description: /report creates a CSV from store.page(0, 1000), which contains every owner's links, and then returns it to any authenticated user. There is no owner or administrator check, so a normal session can obtain other users' codes, targets, owners, and hit counts.

findings.title: User-controlled report name permits path traversal
findings.description: The /report query's name is concatenated into File(dir, name + ".csv") without rejecting separators or parent references. A request such as /report?name=../../tmp/pwned writes the all-users CSV outside the configured export directory and truncates an existing .csv file if the process has permission to write it.

findings.title: Expiry check is inverted, deleting live links and serving expired ones
findings.description: resolve() treats a link as expired when now is BEFORE expiresAt, the opposite of the intended test. Thus normal redirects delete active links, while expired links continue resolving and increment hits until the janitor eventually removes them. This corrupts normal operation and causes loss of active shortenings.

findings.title: Predictable short codes can collide and overwrite links
findings.description: newCode() uses java.util.Random and takes only the first eight hex characters. Generated codes are returned to clients, so sequential outputs are predictable. create() also puts the code into the map without checking for an existing entry, allowing a collision to replace another link and redirect traffic to the attacker's target.

findings.title: Sensitive multi-owner CSV is not forced to owner-only permissions
findings.description: FileWriter creates report files according to the process umask, commonly producing world-readable 0644 files, despite the comment claiming the file is readable only by the service user. An unprivileged local user may therefore read every owner's links and metadata from the export directory.

findings.title: CSV fields are not encoded
findings.description: code, target, and owner are appended directly into the CSV. In particular, owner is attacker-controlled and may begin with '=', '+', '-', or '@' or contain newlines, enabling spreadsheet formula injection when a generated report is opened by support or a dashboard user.
